## Remove the code-generation machinery wholesale: the patch pipeline is an intent… — 2026-07-25 (parent c86c989c9856)

The entire code-generation machinery has been removed; the patch pipeline is now an intent store only, with `record_intent` as the sole apply behaviour. Deleted modules and symbols include:

- `trie/edits/backends/` (`EditRequest`, `EditResult`, `SymbolEditBackend`, `InProcessLLMBackend`, `FakeBackend`, `make_backend`)
- `trie/edits/textgen`, `trie/edits/infer`, `trie/edits/cascade_plan`, `trie/edits/apply`, `trie/edits/report` (including `ApplyReport`, `AppliedItem`, all `STAGE_*` constants)
- `trie/edits/pipeline` functions `stage`, `commit`, `stage_and_commit`, `build_workorder` and all generation helpers
- `LanguageBackend` protocol members `lsp_backends`, `overlay_globs`, `edit_system_prompt`, `code_fence`, `validate_syntax` from Python and TypeScript backends
- `Config` fields `Edits`, `LanguageConfig`, `LspBackend`; `Models.edits` silently ignored for backward compatibility

Surviving: `preview_patches` and `_expand_callers` (moved into the slim pipeline), `session_note_ok` (moved from `report.py` into `pipeline.py`), and `record_intent`. `TrieTools.commit` and `patch_apply_cmd` now call `record_intent` directly with no backend, thread pool, or apply lock.
